artists.biography:
Primal Scream are a Scottish alternative rock band originally formed in 1982 in Glasgow by Bobby Gillespie (vocals) and Jim Beattie and now based in London. The current lineup consists of Gillespie, Andrew Innes (guitar), Martin Duffy (keyboards), and Darrin Mooney (drums). Barrie Cadogan has toured and recorded with the band since 2006 as a replacement after the departure of guitarist Robert "Throb" Young.

The band performed throughout 1982-1984, but their career did not take off until Gillespie left his position as drummer of The Jesus and Mary Chain. The band were a key part of the mid-1980s indie pop scene, but eventually moved away from their more jangly sound, taking on more psychedelic and then garage rock influences, before incorporating a dance music element to their sound. Their 1991 album Screamadelica broke the band into the mainstream. Despite multiple lineup changes, the band has remained commercially successful and continues to tour and record.

perplexity.description:
The Screamadelica 12" Singles" by Primal Scream is a special box set released by Sony Music that compiles the original 12-inch singles from their landmark 1991 album Screamadelica. The original album is a seminal work blending electronic, rock, and funk/soul elements, marking a pivotal moment in the band's evolution by merging club culture with their rock roots. This fusion helped Screamadelica become an era-defining classic, earning critical acclaim including the Mercury Prize and achieving the band's first Top 10 commercial success.

Musically, Screamadelica is noted for its innovative synthesis of psychedelic rock, house music, and soul, with standout singles such as "Movin’ On Up," "Loaded," and "Come Together" that remain influential dancefloor and radio staples. The 12" Singles box set features nine heavyweight vinyl replicas of these singles along with a previously unreleased remix by the album’s late producer Andrew Weatherall, emphasizing the album’s lasting impact on both electronic and rock music scenes. This release celebrates the album’s 30th anniversary, reaffirming its place as a critical and commercial milestone in Primal Scream’s discography.
